static_findings.snippet: `Either<E, A>` is simple: it holds either an error (`E`) or a value (`A`).

content.value_statement: Unchecked exceptions make TypeScript failures difficult to track. This skill teaches practical Either and TaskEither patterns for explicit, composable error handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains Either, Left, and Right through practical TypeScript examples.
Converts throwing functions and nullable values into typed error results.
Chains synchronous and asynchronous operations with Either and TaskEither.
Accumulates multiple validation failures with applicative validation.
Wraps Promise, fetch, database, and schema boundaries with TaskEither.
Models partial success for list and bulk operations.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not install fp-ts or edit projects automatically.
Uses illustrative placeholders that require adaptation to project types and dependencies.
Focuses on fp-ts patterns rather than comparing every TypeScript result library.
Does not replace project-specific testing, observability, or security review.

use_cases.title: Refactor Exception-Based Code
use_cases.description: Replace hidden exceptions with typed Either results and explicit handling paths.

use_cases.title: Design Reliable Service Pipelines
use_cases.description: Compose database and API operations with TaskEither, typed failures, retries, and fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Collect Form Validation Errors
use_cases.description: Build validators that report every field failure instead of stopping after the first error.

prompt_templates.title: Understand Either
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Either, Left, and Right using a simple TypeScript parsing example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learning the basic fp-ts error model

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Throwing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my throwing TypeScript function into Either and explain each error type.

prompt_templates.title: Accumulate Validation Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design fp-ts validation for these fields and return all failures with field-specific messages.

prompt_templates.title: Compose Async Failure Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TaskEither workflow for these API and database steps, including typed errors, retries, fallbacks, and final handling.

output_examples.input: Refactor a JSON parser that currently throws exceptions.
output_examples.output: The response describes an Either-based parser, defines the error channel, and explains how callers handle both outcomes.

output_examples.input: Design validation for email, password, and age fields.
output: A validation plan that preserves field-specific errors.
An explanation of applicative validation for collecting every failure.
Guidance for presenting errors at the form boundary.

output_examples.input: Wrap user loading and related requests with TaskEither.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a lazy asynchronous pipeline, typed transport errors, parallel work, retries, and final result handling.

best_practices: Define precise error types before composing business operations.
Convert exceptions, nullable values, and promises at system boundaries.
Handle both error and success branches once at the edge of the workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not hide failures with broad defaults when callers need error details.
Do not mix unchecked exceptions into an otherwise typed Either pipeline.
Do not retry every failure without limits or error classification.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches practical fp-ts patterns for representing, composing, and handling typed failures in TypeScript.

faq.question: Does this skill install fp-ts?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples for projects that choose fp-ts.

faq.question: When should I use Either?
faq.answer: Use Either for synchronous operations that can return a typed failure or a successful value.

faq.question: When should I use TaskEither?
faq.answer: Use TaskEither for lazy asynchronous operations that can fail, including API and database calls.

faq.question: Can it collect multiple validation errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains applicative validation with NonEmptyArray for accumulating multiple failures.

faq.question: Will the examples work without adaptation?
faq.answer: Not always. Placeholder types, imports, libraries, and project conventions must match the target codebase.
